subject: Midquarter resource rollforward: exec prioritization & dependency asks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midquarter resource rollforward: exec prioritization & dependency asks

Team —

Quick midquarter pulse and an ask for executive direction so we can lock the QBR narrative and downstream commitments. I took the liberty of attaching a short snapshot (midq-resource-snapshot.xlsx) with the current engineering runway and a proposed minimal rollforward across three priority OKRs. High-level notes: 

1) OKR-A (Serving runtime SLOs): we are tracking +5% latency at p95 on long-tail inference when models run with prefix caching disabled for privacy-mode customers. The engineering ask: 2 FW engineers + 1 infra SRE for 8 weeks to land KV cache isolation and a targeted kernel tweak. Without this, we risk missing the SLO improvement target and increased customer support load.

2) OKR-B (Dedicated product adoption): sales-led trials are strong but procurement is the gating factor for two mid-market deals (Acme Analytics and Nimbus Cloud). Legal/procurement needs a dedicated resource to close terms and a short SLA addendum. External procurement reach-outs are in flight (see attached acme-procurement-terms.pdf).

3) OKR-C (Optimize tooling for cost/perf): a scoped quantization pilot could save ~18% token cost but requires an ML engineer and 1 GPU-hour quota from infra for experiments.

Proposed rollforward (short): prioritize OKR-A and OKR-B for the remainder of the quarter. Re-scope OKR-C to a light discovery with deliverables limited to a short eval and cost estimate. If we confirm the rollforward, engineering can reassign two engineers from lower-priority infra work to OKR-A immediately.

Decisions requested from execs by EOD Friday 10/31:
- Greenlight 2 FTE temporary reassignments to OKR-A (FW + SRE).
- Approve prioritization of procurement/legal support for Acme/Nimbus to unblock Dedicated deals.
- Endorse scoped discovery (2-week) for quantization rather than a full pilot.

If we get the go-ahead, I will coordinate with Markus and Vanessa on exact handoffs and publish a revised roadmap to the Drive link below. I’ve set up a 30-minute sync for tomorrow to run through risks and tradeoffs if you’d rather decide with a quick call.

Attachments: midq-resource-snapshot.xlsx, acme-procurement-terms.pdf
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/midq-rollforward-2026

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Midquarter resource rollforward: exec prioritization & dependency asks

Laura —

Thanks for the tight summary and the attachments. I’m broadly supportive of pushing on OKR-A given the SLO risk. A couple of quick clarifying asks before I sign off:

- Can you add the expected delta in incident volume and on-call cost if we do not fund the 2 FTEs?
- For the kernel change, what’s the roll-back plan and the estimated QA window (days)?

If you can drop those two bullets in a one-pager by noon I’ll be comfortable approving the FTE reassignments. Otherwise, I’ll need a short discussion in the sync.

On the procurement front, I’ll nudge legal to expedite the Acme terms review.

– Markus

Appreciate the concise framing, Laura. My view: we should prioritize OKR-B and OKR-A in that order — closing Dedicated trials has immediate revenue and will validate the product-market fit for the Dedicated tier. I can free up two engineers from the capacity optimization effort (their tickets are largely exploratory) to put on OKR-A for the next 6 weeks. That should get us to a safe SLO delta.

On procurement: I will ask Solutions Ops to stand up a procurement packet for Acme and Nimbus and will personally escalate to Nimbus’s procurement lead after lunch. Emma at Acme has been responsive in previous threads (copied below), so we should be able to compress terms review to a week if legal signs the addendum quickly.

If Markus can get me the incident delta numbers, I’ll approve the temporary FTE move and we can publish the QBR narrative.

— Vanessa

- Prioritize procurement support to close Acme and Nimbus (Vanessa to own escalation; Solutions Ops to produce packet).
- Re-scope OKR-C to a two-week discovery with concrete deliverables (Laura to publish success criteria).
